items.title: Morning Briefing: Nov. 14, 2026
items.excerpt: Here's a rundown of all the news you need to know for Saturday, including Türkiye and Qatar signing five agreements, including a mutual defense pact, during the 12th meeting of the Türkiye-Qatar High Strategic Committee in Istanbul; the US Federal Aviation Administration lifting a nationwide flight ground stop after a telecommunications outage; and US President Donald Trump set to hold trilateral talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen next week, according to the White House. Türkiye and Qatar signed five agreements, including a mutual defense pact, during the 12th meeting of the Türkiye-Qatar High Strategic Committee in Istanbul, with the signing ceremony held at the Presidential Dolmabahce Office in the presence of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani. Erdogan and Sheikh Tamim signed the mutual defense agreement, while the other deals cover consumer protection, education, and cooperation on peace, reconciliation and conflict resolution. Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan and Qatari Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani signed the memorandum on peace, reconciliation and conflict resolution, along with a joint declaration marking the committee’s 12th meeting. - US FAA lifts nationwide flight ground stop after telecommunications outage The US Federal Aviation Administration lifted a nationwide ground stop at airports after a telecommunications outage affecting Air Route Traffic Control Centers prompted authorities to halt flights as a precaution, with Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy describing the problem as a "communication issue" and "an emergency." Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters at the White House that the public was "never" in danger and that there was "no indication as of yet that this was a nefarious attack." "We’re not ruling out anything," Mullin said when asked about a possible cyberattack, while the FAA said every flight had been accounted for and international flights would be handled case by case. Separately, Microsoft said it had "no indication" the ground stop was related to any of its services, while FlightAware said more than 10,000 flights were delayed or canceled. - Trump to hold trilateral talks with Xi, Putin in China next week: White House US President Donald Trump will meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen next week on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, with assistant White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales saying he will discuss reducing nuclear weapons, whose proliferation Trump believes is "very dangerous." A senior US official said Washington does not expect an agreement, calling the talks "the entry point, the first conversation" at the leader level, and said Trump plans to raise Iran but not Ukraine because China is not part of the separate US-Russia track. Trump will leave Washington on Monday for Manila for a Quad leaders’ meeting and the US-ASEAN Special Summit, then travel to Shenzhen on Wednesday, where he will hold a meeting and working lunch with Xi on Thursday before the trilateral meeting. Another senior US official described the Trump-Xi session as an "implementation check-in” on the trade agreement, with no tariff changes expected. Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk will join Trump for parts of his visit to China but will not participate in official meetings, according to US officials.

items.title: Wholesale food prices are on the rise
items.excerpt: Food prices are rising sharply even before they reach supermarket shelves. Why it matters: Americans are already paying more for groceries. New inflation data this week suggests that the pressure is not letting up. - Wholesale fresh and dry vegetable prices surged 27% last month, adding to a 31% price jump the previous month. - These are the prices paid by food distributors, grocery chains and other businesses to farmers and other producers for eventual sale to consumers. - Wholesale food prices overall are up 1.7% from a year earlier, ending a three-month streak of annual price declines. Zoom in: Unusually warm weather, crop disease and insect infestations have reduced lettuce and other leafy green harvests in California. - The Iran war, meanwhile, has driven up the cost of fertilizer and fuel, making it more expensive to grow and transport food. - A regional grocery chain recently told Federal Reserve officials that it now costs more to transport a head of lettuce from California than to buy the lettuce itself, citing high diesel fuel prices. - Truck freight costs are up almost 25% over the past year, the largest annual increase since 2022 and on par with the surge seen during the pandemic-era inflation shock. The big picture: It's unclear how much of the surge in producer prices will be passed along to consumers. But steeper price increases were already showing up at supermarket checkout counters last month. - Grocery prices rose 0.4%, the biggest monthly increase in 6 months, driven by higher prices for meat, dairy products and snack foods. - Fresh vegetable prices climbed 2%, including a nearly 8% jump in lettuce prices.

items.title: As higher prices seep into broader economy, Fed officials consider faster hikes | News | griffindailynews.com
items.excerpt: - Nov 14, 2026 ... WASHINGTON — More evidence this week of hot inflation in the U.S. was unpleasant news for the Federal Reserve, not to mention consumers: Rising prices may be spreading beyond the one-time shocks from tariffs and high gas prices into the wider economy, meaning that mortgages, credit cards and other forms of borrowing are likely to become increasingly expensive. Tuesday’s consumer price index report showed broadly rising costs across a range of goods and services, some with little connection to more expensive oil and gas or surging investment in artificial intelligence data centers, another factor blamed for worsening inflation. And there is increasing anxiety among Fed officials that higher oil prices stemming from the Iran war may last longer than previously thought. A key issue debated by Fed policymakers for months has been whether inflation would cool on its own if the Iran war ended and oil prices fell and as the impact of tariffs faded. But government data suggested inflation rose to 4% in October compared with a year ago, up from 3.7% in September, even as gas prices leveled off. The potential consequences of the new inflation data emerged immediately. Two Fed officials suggested Tuesday that the central bank may have to hike its key interest rate more quickly to tame inflation. Bigger or faster hikes by the Fed would mean that buying a house or a car, or paying off a credit card would become a steeper hill to climb, with millions of Americans already struggling to make ends meet. Lorie Logan, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas and a voting member of the Fed’s rate-setting committee, said Tuesday that price increases remain high for services such as “visits to the doctor, childcare, dining out and hotel stays.” “Prices for these services aren’t particularly sensitive to tariffs, conflict in the Middle East or surging demand for computer chips,” she added. “While I expect inflation to moderate as price pressures dissipate in energy and manufactured goods, the broader inflationary trend is more likely to persist.” Logan said Tuesday she supported two additional quarter-point rate hikes. While she has made similar statements before, Logan added that the Fed could “move more rapidly this winter” than it “has moved so far this fall,” signaling that she may support two rate hikes in a row, a quicker pace than the Fed’s current approach. At its last meeting in late October, the central bank kept rates unchanged at about 3.9%. Chairman Kevin Warsh declined to suggest whether more increases were likely. The central bank hiked rates at its September meeting. Wall Street investors now see 90% odds that the Fed will lift borrowing costs at its next meeting Dec. 8-9, according to futures prices tracked by CME Fedwatch. Expectations for a second hike at its January meeting tripled between Monday and Tuesday, to more than 64%. Some Fed officials had expressed optimism over the summer that once the shocks from tariffs and high gas prices faded, inflation would retreat without Fed intervention. But Anna Paulson, president of the Philadelphia Fed, poured cold water on that view in a speech late Tuesday. “Underlying inflation is above target, and it hasn’t come down,” she said. “That tells me that elevated inflation isn’t just about factors that will go away on their own.” Still, she also said she supported only gradual rate increases. Tuesday’s inflation report showed prices rising in many areas with little connection to energy costs or AI, including streaming video services, beef and auto insurance. But surging investment in data centers has driven up the cost of computer chips, power generation equipment, and copper, among other components, with little sign of easing. Prices for smartphones jumped 1.4% just from September to October, the government said, the largest such increase on record. Computer prices leapt 0.5% last month, and television prices rose 3.3%, reversing the more typical trend in which those prices fall with technological innovation.

items.title: Bessent, Fed official divided on role of energy shock in inflation - Gulf Times
items.excerpt: Reuters/ Washington Published on November 14, 2026 | 12:00 AM ... US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Friday that the Federal Reserve should not hike rates because of inflation driven by an "energy supply shock" tied to the Iran war, comments made to CNBC and promptly contradicted on the network by Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee, who said price pressures were building far beyond what could be explained by high oil prices. "I think the Fed should understand that this is an energy supply shock," while the underlying US economy is very strong, Bessent said in an interview on CNBC. "So I think that to hike too much into an energy supply shock when it's coming down, these are very noisy numbers...You know, the Fed's supposed to look into the future, not look in the rearview mirror." Shortly afterwards, the network hosted Goolsbee, a regular guest on CNBC's morning Squawk Box show, who said that inflation was not just due to energy, but had spread to the service sector and areas like medical care that are not usually responsive to the price of oil, and was also elevated through strong demand tied to the AI data centre buildout. "I respect the secretary and I am trying to figure out the same thing he is trying to figure out, which is how persistent is this inflation? The tariff inflation and oil price shock were supposed to have gone away by now and it hasn't," Goolsbee said. "One puzzle is why have those supply shocks been as persistent as they have been. A second thing is if demand is overheating and that is contributing to inflation, that is more worrisome... Services inflation, which is probably not coming from tariffs or oil, is one of the more troubling aspects of the inflation reports we have been getting." While not committing to a rate hike, he said the Fed "has definitely got work to do to continue to reestablish its credibility." ... Research meanwhile opened a ... Because the US is an energy exporter, higher global oil prices can filter through to the economy in the form of higher corporate profits and wages, providing a source of inflation beyond supply issues that can't be easily ignored by the central bank.

items.title: Two days, two senators: a Trump prosecutor warns Democrats that investigating the administration may be “unlawful.”
items.excerpt: What’s new On Thursday, Aaron Reitz, Trump’s U.S. attorney in southern Texas, told Sen. Elissa Slotkin to preserve her records. Her offense: she said Democrats should “go hard on accountability” once they run Congress. Her “‘oversight’ plans seem to have no legitimate legislative purpose and may therefore be unlawful,” he wrote. He accused her of “terrorizing” Trump’s supporters and cited the same two criminal civil-rights laws he cited a day earlier to Sen. Richard Blumenthal, who is asking who paid for Trump’s ballroom. The letter went online before Slotkin even received it, her office said. Slotkin: “There’s no better telltale sign of an authoritarian leader devolving than when they start trying to criminally indict people for the words they say against him.” Why it matters In January, Congress gets the power to subpoena Trump’s government. His prosecutors are already telling the senators who will use it that asking questions could be a crime. - Trump named her first. On November 7 he singled out Slotkin and ordered DOJ “to look into this criminal act, immediately!” - A grand jury already said no to charging her. In February, Trump’s prosecutors asked jurors to indict Slotkin and five other Democrats over a video about illegal orders. They refused. - The attorney general says there’s nothing to see. The same day, Attorney General Todd Blanche said there are no criminal investigations into “words that incoming senators or congressmen have said.” No lawmaker has been charged. “These letters are meritless,” an oversight expert at the Project On Government Oversight said.

items.title: Entertainment news roundup: 14 November 2026 | SVCZZ
items.excerpt: ## Trailers and first looks Sony Pictures Classics has released the official US teaser trailer for Iron Boy, Louis Clichy’s hand-drawn animated feature and winner of the Special Jury Prize in Un Certain Regard at Cannes. The film opens in limited release on 4 December 2026, with a nationwide release on 22 January 2027. Keerthy Suresh plays Savithiri, a lawyer fighting to save her husband, in the trailer for Sathyavan Savithiri, out now ahead of the film’s 20 November 2026 theatrical release. Mysskin plays a major part. Bhuvan Bam is back as Titu Mama in the Dhindora season 2 trailer, with Sanjeeda Sheikh joining the cast as Kavita Mami. The new season premieres on Netflix on 20 November 2026. A young man who moves to Kathmandu to change his life after being unable to succeed in his studies is the subject of Gobar Ganesh, whose trailer is out. The Nepali film is directed by Marichman Shrestha and stars Balchhi and Barsha Siwakoti. It reaches cinemas on Magh 1. Dhiraaj Rajbanshi’s Himalayan Gold has a second trailer out, ahead of its 20 November 2026 cinema release. Sunil Thapa, Karma, Parikshya Limbu and Rahul Mukhia star. Dhanush and Mammootty share the screen for the first time in the OM: Chapter 1 trailer, out now. Rajkumar Periasamy directs, and the film opens in theatres worldwide on 20 November 2026. Christopher Briney and Michelle Randolph star in Clashing Through the Snow, whose first trailer is out. The holiday road-trip romantic comedy, directed by Carlson Young, premieres on Prime Video on 23 November 2026. The 1960 plot to assassinate Fidel Castro during his United Nations visit is the subject of Killing Castro, whose official trailer Lionsgate has released. Produced by Curtis “50 Cent” Jackson and DJ Khaled, it opens in cinemas on 11 December 2026 and arrives on digital on 18 December. D Gukesh, R Praggnanandhaa, R Vaishali, Arjun Erigaisi and Vidit Gujrathi are the subjects of CANDIDATES, a six-episode series whose official trailer Dopamine Media has released. It premieres on the Dopamine Media YouTube channel on 22 November 2026. ## Casting and production Cristiano Ronaldo has begun production on Day 1s, his first television show. The scripted drama follows a fictional elite football agency and comes from UR-Marv, with Ronaldo executive producing and expected to make his acting debut. No platform or release date has been announced. School Spirits has confirmed its season 4 cast, with 12 stars returning and one promoted to series regular. Christian Weissmann, Katharine Isabella, Clara Alexandrova and Briana Buckmaster join as guest stars, and production is under way. Vishwambhara, Chiranjeevi’s fantasy adventure known during production as Mega 156, has begun its regular shoot. The film is directed by Vassishta and produced by UV Creations, and is billed as the costliest film of Chiranjeevi’s career. Isla Fisher and Blake Ritson have joined Al Pacino in Captivated, Dito Montiel’s thriller about the kidnapping of John Paul Getty III, with Jackson Kelly also joining the cast. Production is under way in Calabria and Rome in Italy. Apple TV has promoted Samba Schutte to series regular for Pluribus season 2. His Mr. Diabate returns with an expanded presence after two guest episodes in season 1. No premiere date has been announced. Netflix has announced Pushpak Vimaan, a crime-caper comedy series from Sudip Sharma starring Jaideep Ahlawat, Abhishek Banerjee and Barun Sobti. No premiere date was given with the announcement. Kai Cech is to voice Shanti in Lost in Mandala, the first global animated feature from Nepal’s Incessant Rain Studios. The film is directed by former Disney visual effects supervisor Kiran Bhakta Joshi, with a screenplay by Zack Stentz, and is now in pre-production with no release date announced. MobLand season 3 starts production next week. Helen Mirren confirmed the start on the A Talent for Murder red carpet, with Tom Hardy and Pierce Brosnan returning. The season 2 finale airs on 20 November 2026. Freya Allan is to lead System, a horror film from director Joachim Ronning. Filming is under way in abandoned London Underground stations and tunnels, with Denzel Baidoo and Felix Edwards co-starring. ## Box office and streaming Ramayana: Rise of a Legend has crossed $100 million worldwide in seven days, with Rs 944.55 crore reported by Sacnilk. CNBC TV18 reports it as the first film outside China to reach the mark in 2026. The Kannada dubbed version of Ramayana: Part 1 has crossed Rs 50 crore net in India, the first Bollywood film to do so. It took Rs 48.95 crore in its eight-day opening week plus Rs 1.17 crore on day 9, and the Karnataka gross across all languages has passed Rs 100 crore. Paper Tiger has debuted at 85 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 114 reviews. The James Gray crime drama stars Adam Driver, Miles Teller and Scarlett Johansson, and opened in limited release on 13 November 2026. Hulu has set 13 January 2027 as the premiere date for The Spot, an A24 psychological thriller starring Claire Danes and Ewan McGregor as a surgeon and her schoolteacher husband who suspect she caused a child’s hit-and-run death. First-look images were released on 12 November 2026. ... Christian Cousins, who played Dominic Palmieri in Kindergarten Cop alongside his twin brother Joseph, has died aged 43.
